title: 10. Exercises: Dataclasses, Enum & Pydantic Masterclass
summary: You now have COMPLETE mastery of Python Dataclasses, Enum, and Pydantic!
objectives: Solve the Dataclasses, Enum & Pydantic Masterclass exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: What is a Dataclass? — Coding Challenges (Chapter 1 — Dataclass Basics)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Create a "Library Book Management" system using dataclasses:
  - Book dataclass: ISBN, title, author, year, genre, available (bool)
  - Library dataclass: name, books (List[Book])
  - Methods: add_book, remove_book, find_by_author, find_by_genre
  - Auto-generate: book_id from ISBN, display_title as "Title by Author"
  - Sort books by year, then title
  - Equality based on ISBN only

CHALLENGE 2:
  Build a "Student Grade Tracker":
  - Student dataclass: student_id, name, email, courses (List[str])
  - Grade dataclass: student_id, course, score (float), letter_grade
  - Auto-compute letter_grade in __post_init__ from score
  - GradeBook: list of grades with methods:
    * average_for_student(student_id)
    * top_students(n, course)
    * failing_students() → score < 60
  - Sort grades by score descending

CHALLENGE 3:
  Design an "E-commerce Cart" system:
  - CartItem: product_id, name, price, quantity, discount_percent (default 0)
  - Property: discounted_price, total
  - Cart: customer_id, items, coupon_code (optional)
  - Methods: add_item, remove_item, apply_discount
  - Properties: subtotal, tax (10%), total, item_count
  - Validation: quantity > 0, price >= 0, discount 0-100

CHALLENGE 4:
  Create a "Weather Station" data model:
  - Reading dataclass: timestamp, temperature, humidity, pressure, wind_speed
  - Validation: temperature -90 to 60 C, humidity 0-100, pressure 870-1084 hPa
  - WeatherStation: station_id, location, readings (List[Reading])
  - Methods: average_temp(days), max_temp, min_temp, readings_above_temp(threshold)
  - frozen=True for immutable readings
  - Sorting by timestamp

CHALLENGE 5:
  Build a "Job Application Tracker":
  - Company: name, industry, size (small/medium/large), remote_friendly
  - JobPosting: job_id, title, company, salary_min, salary_max, required_skills
  - Application: app_id, job, status, applied_date, notes
  - Statuses: applied → screening → interview → offer → rejected
  - Methods: days_since_applied, is_active, salary_midpoint
  - Sort by: salary_max, then company name

CHALLENGE 6:
  Implement a "Bank Account" system:
  - Transaction: transaction_id, type (deposit/withdraw), amount, timestamp, balance_after
  - Account: account_id, owner, account_type, transactions (List[Transaction])
  - Properties: current_balance, total_deposits, total_withdrawals
  - Methods: deposit(amount), withdraw(amount), statement(n_recent)
  - Validation: amount > 0, sufficient funds for withdrawal
  - frozen=True for Transaction (audit trail!)

CHALLENGE 7:
  Design a "Recipe Manager":
  - Ingredient: name, quantity, unit, calories_per_unit
  - NutritionInfo: calories, protein, carbs, fat (all per serving)
  - Recipe: recipe_id, name, servings, ingredients, prep_time, cook_time
  - Properties: total_time, calories_per_serving, ingredient_count
  - Methods: scale_for_servings(n), find_high_calorie_ingredients(threshold)
  - Comparison: recipes by calories_per_serving (order=True)
  - Use asdict() to export recipe to dict/JSON
```

sections.title: Field Definitions & the field() Function — Coding Challenges (Chapter 2 — field())
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build a "Survey Form Generator":
  - Use field(metadata=...) to define form field properties
  - Metadata: label, placeholder, required, type, validation rules
  - Function: generate_html_form(dataclass) → HTML string
  - Support types: text, number, email, date, select, checkbox
  - Generate: JSON schema from field metadata
  - Validate form submission against field metadata rules

CHALLENGE 2:
  Create a "Multi-Currency Transaction" model:
  - Fields: from_account, to_account, amount (kw_only), currency (kw_only)
  - init=False computed fields: transaction_id, timestamp, status
  - repr=False fields: from_account_token, to_account_token
  - compare=False fields: processing_time, retry_count
  - default_factory for: audit_log list, metadata dict
  - __post_init__: validate amount > 0, generate transaction_id

CHALLENGE 3:
  Design a "Machine Learning Feature Set":
  - Feature dataclass with field metadata for ML pipelines:
    {"scaling": "standard", "encoding": "one_hot", "imputation": "mean"}
  - FeatureSet: features list, target column, split ratio
  - init=False: feature_count, categorical_features, numerical_features
  - Function: generate_preprocessing_pipeline(feature_set)
  - Function: validate_schema(data_dict, feature_set)

CHALLENGE 4:
  Implement a "Database Schema Generator":
  - Extend the db_field() example to support full SQL generation
  - Support: foreign keys, indexes, check constraints
  - Generate: CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, INSERT statements
  - Introspect fields with fields() to build queries dynamically
  - Support: relationships (one-to-many, many-to-many)
  - Generate: ORM-style query methods (find_by_field, find_all)

CHALLENGE 5:
  Create an "API Contract Validator":
  - Dataclass with field metadata describing API contract:
    {"api_name": "user_id", "required": True, "type": "integer"}
  - Function: validate_request(data_dict, contract_class)
  - Function: validate_response(response_dict, contract_class)
  - Report: missing fields, wrong types, constraint violations
  - Generate: OpenAPI/Swagger schema from dataclass + metadata
  - Support: nested models, arrays, optional fields

CHALLENGE 6:
  Build a "Configuration Validator":
  - Config dataclass with field metadata:
    {"env_var": "DB_HOST", "required": True, "sensitive": True}
  - Load from: environment variables, .env file, config.json
  - Priority: env vars > config file > field defaults
  - Validate: required fields present, types match, constraints
  - Mask sensitive fields in logs (repr=False + metadata["sensitive"])
  - Generate: .env.example file from field metadata

CHALLENGE 7:
  Design a "Report Builder":
  - ReportColumn: name, type, metadata with format/aggregation info
    {"format": "currency", "aggregation": "sum", "visible": True}
  - ReportDefinition: columns, filters, sort_by, page_size
  - init=False: generated_at, column_count, visible_columns
  - Function: format_cell(value, column) using metadata
  - Function: aggregate_column(data, column) using metadata
  - Function: generate_csv_header(report) from visible columns
```

sections.title: Dataclass Parameters — Coding Challenges (Chapter 3 — Parameters)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build an "Immutable Money Value Object":
  - frozen=True Money dataclass: amount (Decimal), currency (str)
  - Operations: add, subtract, multiply (return new Money instances)
  - Compare: ==, <, > (only same currency!)
  - Convert between currencies using a rate dict
  - Format: "USD 1,234.56" or "EUR 1.234,56"
  - Use in a set to deduplicate a list of Money values

CHALLENGE 2:
  Create a "Type-Safe Event System":
  - frozen=True events: UserCreated, OrderPlaced, PaymentProcessed
  - Each event: event_id, timestamp (auto), aggregate_id
  - EventStore: stores events as frozen immutable records
  - query: by aggregate_id, by time range, by event type
  - Replay: apply events in order to reconstruct state
  - Use event as dict key for deduplication

CHALLENGE 3:
  Implement a "High-Performance Log Parser":
  - slots=True, frozen=True LogEntry: timestamp, level, service, message
  - Parse 1 million log lines into LogEntry objects
  - Profile: memory vs regular dataclass
  - Group by: service, level, hour
  - Filter: error entries, specific service
  - Export to CSV efficiently

CHALLENGE 4:
  Design a "Semantic Version Manager":
  - frozen=True, order=True SemVer with full comparison
  - Support: 1.2.3, 1.2.3-beta.1, 1.2.3+build.123
  - Operations: bump_major/minor/patch, is_compatible
  - VersionRange: ">=1.0.0, <2.0.0" — check if version satisfies
  - Package: name, version, dependencies (list of VersionRange)
  - Resolve: find compatible versions for all packages

CHALLENGE 5:
  Build a "GPS Track Analyzer":
  - frozen=True, order=True GeoPoint: lat, lon, elevation, timestamp
  - Track: ordered list of GeoPoints
  - Calculate: total distance, elevation gain/loss, duration
  - Find: highest point, lowest point, fastest segment
  - Segment: split track by time gaps or distance
  - Export: to GPX format (XML)

CHALLENGE 6:
  Create a "Tournament Bracket System":
  - order=True Team: wins, losses, points, name
  - Match: team1, team2, scores (frozen=True)
  - Tournament: teams, matches, rounds
  - Standings: sort teams by points, then wins, then name
  - Bracket: generate elimination bracket
  - Stats: top scorer team, undefeated teams, head-to-head

CHALLENGE 7:
  Implement a "Memory-Efficient Particle Simulator":
  - slots=True Particle: x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, mass, charge
  - Create 1 million particles
  - Update positions: particle.x += particle.vx * dt
  - Calculate forces between nearby particles
  - Compare memory: slots vs regular vs numpy
  - Profile and optimize the hot loop
```

CHALLENGE 4:
Design a "Network Connection Pool":

- Connection: host, port, InitVar[credentials] (auth, store token not creds)
- ClassVar: \_pool dict, MAX_CONNECTIONS (10), \_active_count
- **post_init**: authenticate, add to pool, enforce max limit

- ConnectionPool manager: get, release, close_all, health_check

CHALLENGE 5:
Build a "Financial Audit Trail":

- AuditEntry: action, entity_id, InitVar[actor_token] (verify, store actor_id)
- ClassVar: \_audit_log list, \_checksums set (tamper detection)
- **post_init**: verify token, compute checksum of previous entry + this

CHALLENGE 6:

- **post_init**: load dataset stats (rows, features, class distribution)

sections.title: Inheritance in Dataclasses — Coding Challenges (Chapter 5 — Inheritance)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build a "Content Management System":
  - BaseContent: id, author, created_at, status (draft/published/archived)
  - Article(BaseContent): title, body, tags, word_count (computed)
  - Video(BaseContent): title, url, duration_seconds, thumbnail_url
  - Podcast(BaseContent): title, audio_url, transcript, episode_number
  - Comment(BaseContent): parent_content_id, body, likes
  - ContentRepository: CRUD for all content types, filter by type/status

CHALLENGE 2:
  Design an "Employee Hierarchy System":
  - Employee: id, name, email, department, salary, hire_date
  - Manager(Employee): direct_reports (List[Employee]), budget
  - Developer(Employee): skills (List[str]), level (junior/mid/senior)
  - SalesRep(Employee): territory, quota, commission_rate
  - Executive(Manager): compensation_package, board_member (bool)
  - Methods: annual_cost(), performance_review(), org_chart()

CHALLENGE 3:
  Implement a "Financial Instrument Hierarchy":
  - FinancialInstrument: symbol, name, market, currency
  - Stock(Instrument): shares_outstanding, dividend_yield, pe_ratio
  - Bond(Instrument): face_value, coupon_rate, maturity_date, rating
  - ETF(Instrument): holdings (List), expense_ratio, aum
  - Option(Instrument): underlying, strike, expiry, option_type (call/put)
  - Portfolio: mix of instruments, calculate: value, risk, diversification

CHALLENGE 4:
  Create a "Database Query Builder":
  - BaseQuery: table, conditions, limit, offset
  - SelectQuery(Base): columns, joins, order_by, group_by
  - InsertQuery(Base): values (dict)
  - UpdateQuery(Base): updates (dict), where_required validation
  - DeleteQuery(Base): where_required validation (no empty where!)
  - Each: to_sql(), to_parameterized(), validate()

CHALLENGE 5:
  Build a "Game Entity System":
  - Entity: id, name, position (x,y), health, max_health
  - Character(Entity): level, experience, inventory (List)
  - Player(Character): username, score, lives, controls
  - NPC(Character): ai_type, patrol_path, dialogue
  - Boss(NPC): phase, special_attacks, drops (List)
  - Enemy(NPC): aggro_range, damage, loot_table
  - Combat: calculate_damage, apply_effects, check_death

CHALLENGE 6:
  Design a "Sensor Data Pipeline":
  - Sensor: sensor_id, location, unit, calibration_date
  - TemperatureSensor(Sensor): min_temp, max_temp, precision
  - HumiditySensor(Sensor): min_humidity, max_humidity
  - PressureSensor(Sensor): baseline_pressure, altitude_compensation
  - CompoundSensor(Sensor): sensors List[Sensor] (contains multiple)
  - Reading: sensor, raw_value, calibrated_value (computed), timestamp
  - SensorNetwork: register, read_all, detect_anomalies, export_csv

CHALLENGE 7:
  Implement a "Testing Framework":
  - TestCase: name, description, timeout, tags
  - UnitTest(TestCase): function to test, mock_dependencies
  - IntegrationTest(TestCase): services_required, setup_db, teardown_db
  - PerformanceTest(TestCase): iterations, target_ms, memory_limit_mb
  - TestSuite: collection of TestCases, run_all, run_by_tag
  - TestResult: test_case, status (pass/fail/skip/error), duration, error_msg
  - Report: generate summary, export to JSON/HTML
```

sections.title: Advanced Dataclass Features — Coding Challenges (Chapter 6 — Advanced Features)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build a "Universal Dataclass ORM":
  - Use fields() to generate SQL CREATE TABLE
  - Use asdict() to generate INSERT/UPDATE SQL
  - from_dict() to hydrate objects from DB rows
  - Support: primary keys, foreign keys (from metadata)
  - Query builder: select, filter, order, limit using dataclass fields
  - Connection pool: execute queries and return dataclass instances

CHALLENGE 2:
  Create a "State Machine Framework":
  - Use frozen dataclasses for immutable states
  - Use replace() for state transitions
  - Define transitions as dataclasses (from_state, to_state, action)
  - Validate transitions against allowed rules
  - History: keep full state history for undo
  - Export: state diagram as ASCII art

CHALLENGE 3:
  Implement a "Dataclass Diff Engine":
  - Compare two instances of same dataclass using fields()
  - Find: changed fields, added fields, removed fields (for inheritance)
  - Generate: human-readable diff report
  - Generate: patch dict to transform instance1 into instance2
  - Apply: patch to create new instance using replace()
  - Support: nested dataclass comparison (recursive diff)

CHALLENGE 4:
  Build a "Dynamic Form Validation System":
  - Load form schema from JSON config file
  - Use make_dataclass() to create validation class
  - Validate submitted form data against schema
  - Support: required/optional, type coercion, regex, range
  - Generate: error messages per field
  - Cache: created classes for reuse (avoid recreation)

CHALLENGE 5:
  Create a "Versioned Configuration Manager":
  - Config as frozen dataclass (immutable)
  - Replace() to create new version on each change
  - Keep history of all config versions with timestamps
  - Diff between any two versions using fields()
  - Rollback to any previous version
  - Export config history to JSON for audit

CHALLENGE 6:
  Implement a "CSV Schema Inferencer":
  - Read CSV file
  - Detect column types (int, float, bool, str, date)
  - Use make_dataclass() to create a typed dataclass
  - Parse all CSV rows into typed dataclass instances
  - Validate: nulls, type mismatches, range outliers
  - Export: inferred schema as Python code (actual @dataclass definition)

CHALLENGE 7:
  Build a "Data Pipeline Transformer":
  - Source dataclass: raw data schema (from API/CSV)
  - Target dataclass: clean data schema (for DB)
  - Mapping config: source_field → target_field + transformation
  - Use fields() to discover source fields automatically
  - Apply transformations: rename, type-cast, compute, split, join
  - Use replace()/from_dict() to create target instances
  - Report: transformation stats, errors, data quality metrics
```

sections.title: What is Enum? — Coding Challenges (Chapter 7 — Basic Enum)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build a "Restaurant Order System":
  - FoodCategory Enum: APPETIZER, MAIN, DESSERT, DRINK, SPECIAL
  - OrderStatus Enum: with valid transitions, is_kitchen_active property
  - TableStatus Enum: AVAILABLE, OCCUPIED, RESERVED, CLEANING
  - MenuItem dataclass: name, category (Enum), price, available
  - Order dataclass: table, items, status (Enum)
  - Methods: add_item, remove_item, transition_status, calculate_total

CHALLENGE 2:
  Create a "Git-like Version Control States":
  - FileStatus Enum: UNTRACKED, STAGED, MODIFIED, COMMITTED, DELETED
  - BranchType Enum: MAIN, FEATURE, HOTFIX, RELEASE, EXPERIMENTAL
  - MergeStatus Enum: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, MERGED, CONFLICTED, ABORTED
  - Commit dataclass: hash, message, status, branch, author
  - Repository: track files by status, branch operations

CHALLENGE 3:
  Design a "Network Protocol Handler":
  - Protocol Enum: HTTP, HTTPS, WS, WSS, FTP, SMTP — with default ports
  - HTTPMethod Enum: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS
  - StatusCode Enum: groups by range (2xx success, 4xx client, 5xx server)
  - Request dataclass: method (Enum), url, protocol (Enum), headers, body
  - Response dataclass: status (Enum), body, headers
  - Methods: is_success, is_error, requires_body

CHALLENGE 4:
  Implement a "CI/CD Pipeline":
  - PipelineStatus Enum: QUEUED, RUNNING, PASSING, FAILING, CANCELLED
  - StageType Enum: BUILD, TEST, LINT, SECURITY, DEPLOY, NOTIFY
  - Environment Enum: DEV, STAGING, UAT, PRODUCTION — with properties
  - Stage dataclass: type, status, duration, logs
  - Pipeline: stages, overall_status (computed), can_deploy property
  - Rules: PRODUCTION deployment requires PASSING status in all stages

CHALLENGE 5:
  Build a "Trading Platform":
  - OrderType Enum: MARKET, LIMIT, STOP, STOP_LIMIT, TRAILING_STOP
  - OrderSide Enum: BUY, SELL — with opposite() method
  - OrderStatus Enum: with is_active, is_filled, can_cancel properties
  - TimeInForce Enum: GTC, DAY, IOC, FOK — with descriptions
  - Trade dataclass: symbol, type, side, quantity, price, status, time_in_force
  - Validation: each order type has specific required fields

CHALLENGE 6:
  Create a "Hospital Workflow System":
  - PatientStatus Enum: WAITING, TRIAGE, CONSULTATION, TREATMENT, DISCHARGED
  - Priority Enum: NON_URGENT, SEMI_URGENT, URGENT, EMERGENCY, RESUSCITATION
  - Department Enum: with specialty, floor, max_patients properties
  - Bed Enum: AVAILABLE, OCCUPIED, MAINTENANCE, RESERVED
  - Patient dataclass: status (Enum), priority (Enum), department (Enum)
  - Scheduler: assign_patient, transfer, discharge, calculate_wait_time

CHALLENGE 7:
  Implement a "Multi-Language Localization System":
  - Language Enum: with locale code, native name, direction (LTR/RTL), currency
  - Country Enum: with capital, language, timezone, calling code
  - TextDirection Enum: LTR, RTL — with CSS property
  - Locale dataclass: language (Enum), country (Enum), date_format, number_format
  - Translator: translate text using Enum keys, format dates/numbers per locale
  - Fallback chain: try exact locale, then language, then English
```

sections.title: Enum Types — Coding Challenges (Chapter 8 — Enum Types)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build a "Unix File Permission System":
  - Permission(IntFlag): READ=4, WRITE=2, EXECUTE=1
  - PermissionSet: owner, group, other (each is Permission)
  - Parse chmod notation: "rwxr-xr--" → PermissionSet
  - Parse octal notation: 755 → PermissionSet
  - Generate chmod command from PermissionSet
  - Check: can_read(user_type), can_write, can_execute

CHALLENGE 2:
  Create an "HTTP Client with Status Codes":
  - HTTPMethod(StrEnum): GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
  - HTTPStatus(IntEnum): complete list with categories
  - Properties: is_success, is_redirect, is_client_error, is_server_error
  - Request: method (StrEnum), url, headers, body
  - Response: status (IntEnum), body, headers
  - retry_strategy(status): determine if/how to retry

CHALLENGE 3:
  Implement a "Feature Toggle System":
  - Feature(Flag): all features as combinable flags
  - Plan(IntEnum): FREE=1, PRO=2, ENTERPRISE=3 with ordering
  - Each Plan has a set of included Features
  - User: plan, extra_features (granted individually)
  - check_feature(user, feature) → bool
  - upgrade_plan(user, new_plan) → delta features gained/lost

CHALLENGE 4:
  Design an "Audio/Video Codec System":
  - VideoCodec(StrEnum): H264, H265, VP9, AV1, MPEG4
  - AudioCodec(StrEnum): AAC, MP3, OPUS, FLAC, WAV
  - Container(StrEnum): MP4, MKV, WebM, AVI, MOV
  - Quality(IntEnum): LOW=360, SD=480, HD=720, FHD=1080, UHD=4320
  - Compatibility matrix: which codecs work with which containers
  - MediaConfig: validate codec+container combinations are compatible

CHALLENGE 5:
  Build a "Network Packet Analyzer":
  - Protocol(IntEnum): ICMP=1, TCP=6, UDP=17, HTTP=80, HTTPS=443
  - PacketFlag(IntFlag): SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH, URG (TCP flags)
  - Direction(StrEnum): INBOUND, OUTBOUND, INTERNAL
  - Packet: protocol, flags (PacketFlag), source, destination, size
  - Analyzer: detect port scans (many SYN, no ACK), floods, anomalies

CHALLENGE 6:
  Create a "Game Item System":
  - Rarity(IntEnum): COMMON=1, UNCOMMON=2, RARE=3, EPIC=4, LEGENDARY=5
  - ItemType(Flag): WEAPON, ARMOR, POTION, QUEST_ITEM, STACKABLE, TRADEABLE
  - Slot(StrEnum): HEAD, CHEST, HANDS, LEGS, FEET, MAIN_HAND, OFF_HAND
  - Item: name, rarity, type (Flag), slot, stats
  - Inventory: add, remove, filter by rarity/type, sort by rarity
  - Loot table: generate random item based on rarity weights

CHALLENGE 7:
  Implement a "Cloud Resource Manager":
  - ResourceState(IntEnum): CREATING=1, RUNNING=2, STOPPING=3, STOPPED=4, ERROR=5
  - ResourceType(StrEnum): VM, DATABASE, STORAGE, NETWORK, FUNCTION, QUEUE
  - Region(StrEnum): US_EAST, US_WEST, EU_CENTRAL, AP_SOUTHEAST — with properties
  - Capability(Flag): AUTOSCALE, BACKUP, MONITORING, ENCRYPTION, HA
  - Resource: type, state, region, capabilities (Flag)
  - CloudManager: provision, start, stop, list_by_state/type/region
```

sections.title: What is Pydantic? — Coding Challenges (Chapter 11 — Pydantic Basics)
sections.body:
```
CHALLENGE 1:
  Build a "User Registration System":
  - RegisterRequest: username, email, password, confirm_password, age
  - Validate: username unique format, email format, password match
  - Auto-coerce: age from string, email to lowercase
  - UserResponse: exclude password, add user_id, created_at
  - Simulate: registration → login → profile retrieval flow
  - Error handling: field-by-field error messages for frontend

CHALLENGE 2:
  Create a "Product Catalog Parser":
  - Parse products from 3 different source formats (JSON, CSV-like dict, legacy)
  - Each format has different field names (use aliases)
  - Messy data: prices as strings, quantities as floats, dates in various formats
  - Normalize to single ProductModel with clean types
  - Report: how many parsed successfully, how many failed, which fields failed

CHALLENGE 3:
  Design a "Configuration File Loader":
  - AppConfig: database, cache, api, logging sections (nested models)
  - Load from: JSON file, environment variables, CLI args (dict)

# 📊 COMPLETE MASTER CHEAT SHEET

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║        DATACLASSES + ENUM + PYDANTIC — COMPLETE REFERENCE                  ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  DATACLASSES                                                                 ║
║  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  ║
║  @dataclass                   → basic dataclass                              ║
║  @dataclass(frozen=True)      → immutable + hashable                        ║
║  @dataclass(order=True)       → adds < > <= >= comparison                   ║
║  @dataclass(slots=True)       → memory efficient (Python 3.10+)             ║
║  @dataclass(kw_only=True)     → all fields keyword-only                     ║
║                                                                              ║
║  field() parameters:                                                         ║
║    default=          → default value                                         ║
║    default_factory=  → callable() for mutable defaults (ALWAYS use for list)║
║    init=False        → not in __init__, set in __post_init__                 ║
║    repr=False        → hide from __repr__ (passwords, tokens)                ║
║    compare=False     → exclude from __eq__ and ordering                      ║
║    kw_only=True      → keyword-only this field                               ║
║    metadata={}       → read-only extra info for libraries                    ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Special methods:                                                             ║
║    __post_init__()   → runs after __init__, use for validation/computed      ║
║    InitVar[T]        → pass to __init__/__post_init__ but don't store        ║
║    ClassVar[T]       → class-level, NOT a dataclass field                    ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Utility functions:                                                           ║
║    asdict(obj)       → dataclass → dict (deep)                               ║
║    astuple(obj)      → dataclass → tuple (deep)                              ║
║    fields(cls)       → tuple of Field objects                                ║
║    replace(obj, **changes) → create modified copy                            ║
║    make_dataclass()  → create dataclass at runtime                           ║
║    is_dataclass(obj) → check if dataclass                                    ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  ENUM                                                                        ║
║  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  ║
║  Enum            → base class, strict (RED != 1, RED != "RED")              ║
║  IntEnum         → members ARE ints (OK: 1, SORTED, MATH)                   ║
║  StrEnum         → members ARE strings (Python 3.11+)                       ║
║  (str, Enum)     → string behavior (Python < 3.11)                          ║
║  Flag            → combinable with | (permissions!)                          ║
║  IntFlag         → Flag + integer support                                     ║
║  auto()          → auto-assign values                                         ║
║  @unique          → raise error on duplicate values                           ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Access:                                                                      ║
║    Color.RED       → member by attribute                                     ║
║    Color['RED']    → member by name string                                   ║
║    Color(1)        → member by value                                          ║
║    .name           → 'RED' (string name)                                     ║
║    .value          → 1 (assigned value)                                      ║
║    list(Color)     → all members                                              ║
║    Color.__members__→ dict of all members including aliases                  ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Flag operations:                                                             ║
║    A | B          → combine (READ | WRITE)                                   ║
║    A & B          → intersection                                              ║
║    ~A             → complement (remove)                                       ║
║    A in B         → check if A is set in B                                   ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  PYDANTIC V2                                                                 ║
║  ────────────────────────────────────────────��─────────────────────────────  ║
║  class MyModel(BaseModel):                                                   ║
║      field: type = Field(...)                                                ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Field() constraints:                                                         ║
║    gt/ge/lt/le     → number comparisons                                      ║
║    min_length       → min string/list length                                  ║
║    max_length       → max string/list length                                  ║
║    pattern         → regex pattern                                            ║
║    multiple_of     → must be multiple of N                                   ║
║    decimal_places  → for Decimal fields                                      ║
║    alias           → different name in JSON                                  ║
║    exclude=True    → never in model_dump()                                   ║
║    repr=False      → hide from repr                                          ║
║                                                                              ║
║  model_config = ConfigDict(                                                  ║
║    strict=True         → no type coercion                                    ║
║    from_attributes=True→ read from ORM object attributes                     ║
║    extra="forbid"      → reject unknown fields                               ║
║    frozen=True         → immutable + hashable                                ║
║    use_enum_values=True→ store .value not enum member                        ║
║    str_strip_whitespace→ auto-strip strings                                  ║
║    populate_by_name=True→ accept field name AND alias                        ║
║  )                                                                           ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Validators:                                                                  ║
║    @field_validator("field", mode="before"/"after")                         ║
║    @classmethod                                                               ║
║    def validate(cls, v, info): ...   # raise ValueError or return v         ║
║                                                                              ║
║    @model_validator(mode="before"/"after")                                  ║
║    def validate_model(self): ...     # access self.field_name               ║

║  Serialization:                                                               ║
║    model_dump()           → dict (Python types)                              ║
║    model_dump(mode="json")→ dict (JSON-serializable types)                  ║
║    model_dump_json()      → JSON string (fastest!)                           ║
║    model_dump(include/exclude/exclude_none/exclude_defaults)                 ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Deserialization:                                                             ║
║    Model.model_validate(dict)     → from dict                               ║
║    Model.model_validate_json(str) → from JSON string                        ║
║    Model.model_validate(orm_obj)  → from ORM (from_attributes=True)         ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Other:                                                                       ║
║    model_copy(update={})  → modified copy                                    ║
║    model_json_schema()    → JSON Schema dict                                 ║
║    @computed_field        → derived field (in dump, not init)                ║
║                                                                              ║
║  V1 → V2 Migration:                                                          ║
║    @validator          → @field_validator                                    ║
║    @root_validator     → @model_validator                                    ║
║    class Config        → model_config = ConfigDict(...)                      ║
║    .dict()             → .model_dump()                                       ║
║    .json()             → .model_dump_json()                                  ║
║    .parse_obj()        → .model_validate()                                   ║
║    orm_mode=True       → from_attributes=True                                ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  WHEN TO USE WHAT?                                                           ║
║  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  ║
║  Dataclass  → internal domain objects, pure Python, fast, no validation     ║
║  Enum       → fixed set of named constants, state machines, permissions     ║
║  Pydantic   → API boundaries, user input, config, external data parsing     ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Combine all three:                                                          ║
║  Enum       → define status values (OrderStatus.PENDING)                    ║
║  Dataclass  → internal domain logic (frozen Order with Enum fields)         ║

╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

# 🎯 TOP 30 INTERVIEW QUESTIONS QUICK FIRE

```
DATACLASSES:
Q: What does @dataclass auto-generate?
A: __init__, __repr__, __eq__ (by default)

Q: Why use field(default_factory=list) not default=[]?
A: Mutable default shared across all instances — classic Python bug

Q: What is __post_init__?
A: Called after __init__, used for validation and computed fields

Q: frozen=True gives you what?
A: Immutability + __hash__ (can be used as dict key/in sets)

Q: InitVar vs regular field?
A: InitVar: passed to __init__/__post_init__ but NOT stored as attribute

Q: ClassVar vs regular field?
A: ClassVar: belongs to class, NOT treated as dataclass field (not in init/repr/eq)

Q: asdict() vs vars()?
A: asdict(): deep recursive dict, handles nested dataclasses; vars(): shallow, namespace dict

Q: replace() vs creating new instance?
A: replace(): copies unchanged fields automatically, runs __post_init__

ENUM:
Q: Enum.RED == "red"?
A: False! Regular Enum not equal to its value. Use IntEnum/StrEnum for that.

Q: How access member by value?
A: Color("red") or Color(1) — raises ValueError if not found

Q: What is auto()?
A: Auto-assigns values (default: 1,2,3...). Customize with _generate_next_value_

Q: Flag vs Enum?
A: Flag: members combinable with | for multiple simultaneous states (permissions)

Q: @unique decorator?
A: Prevents duplicate values — raises ValueError if two members have same value

Q: IntEnum gives you what extra?
A: Integer operations: <, >, sorting, arithmetic, == with ints

PYDANTIC:
Q: Pydantic vs dataclass main difference?
A: Pydantic validates types + coerces; dataclass just stores, no validation

Q: mode="before" vs "after" in validator?
A: before: raw input, good for parsing; after: typed value, good for business rules

Q: @field_validator vs @model_validator?
A: field: single field; model: cross-field access (password==confirm)

Q: extra="forbid" vs "ignore" vs "allow"?
A: forbid: error on unknown; ignore: drop silently; allow: keep in __pydantic_extra__

Q: from_attributes=True when?
A: When reading from ORM objects (SQLAlchemy) instead of dicts

Q: model_dump() vs model_dump(mode="json")?
A: mode="json": datetime→str, Decimal→float, ready for json.dumps()

Q: model_copy(update={}) vs model_validate()?
A: copy: fast, partial update of existing model; validate: full parse from external data

Q: Generic model syntax?
A: class Response(BaseModel, Generic[T]): data: T  → Response[UserModel]

Q: Discriminated union what/why?
A: Pick model by literal field value — faster and better errors than trying each

Q: frozen=True in Pydantic config?
A: Immutable instances, enables __hash__, use model_copy for changes

Q: computed_field decorator?
A: Property included in model_dump() output — derived/calculated values

Q: exclude_unset=True in model_dump()?
A: Only include fields explicitly set — perfect for PATCH endpoints

Q: field_validator return value?
A: MUST return the value (transformed or original). No return = None field!

Q: ValidationError fields?
A: .errors() → list of {loc, msg, type, input}; .error_count() → int

Q: How to validate password==confirm_password?
A: @model_validator(mode="after") — access self.password and self.confirm_password

Q: StrEnum vs (str, Enum)?
A: StrEnum = Python 3.11+; (str, Enum) = any Python 3.x version, same behavior
```
